To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
USP36 controls p62/SQTM1-dependent selective autophagic degradation of ubiquitinated protein aggregates.

1) the deubiquitinase USP36 controls p62-mediated selective autophagy; 2) USP36 loss of function activates autophagy and inhibits cell growth; and 3) USP36 function is conserved between Drosophila melanogaster and human cells.
USP36 is a novel, crucial regulator of selective autophagy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of autophagy and its control in Drosophilla and human cells.
the regulation of selective autophagy and the identification of novel regulators of this process.
understanding how the ubiquitin-proteasome system and autophagy pathways are regulated in Drosophilia and human cells.

USP36 is a deubiquitinase that regulates p62/SQTM1-dependent selective autophagic degradation of ubiquitinated substrata.
the deubiqitination enzyme USP36 is required for the selective autophagy of ubiquitinated substratess.
USP36 controls the degradation of specific substrates by selective autophagy in Drosophilla and human cells.

the deubiqutinating enzyme USP 36 controls selective autphagy by regulating p62 function.
